answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a reputation prism: each identity's trust score is projected through a mirror of peer attestations over its verified work, and it decays unless refreshed by fresh verifiable tasks. A new clone starts at zero and dormant identities shed score steadily, so copying old accounts gains nothing. An attacker must pay the real cost of continuously performing genuine work per identity, making sybils unprofitable and leaving the network a haven for honest, active agents.
